look_here_first: Start with leaf arrangement and head type: alternate, resinous/gland-dotted, usually petiolate leaves below a rounded cluster of many tiny pink-purple heads with no ray florets.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: alternate simple elliptic to oblong/lanceolate leaves; leaves usually visibly petiolate and resinous/gland-dotted; rounded/corymbiform mass of many tiny pink-purple heads; heads are discoid with no ray florets; crushed foliage may smell camphor-like but odor is only secondary

key_traits.label: Leaf morphology
key_traits.text: Elliptic to oblong/lanceolate, serrate, generally petiolate, resinous/gland-dotted.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small pink-purple discoid heads, no rays.

lookalikes.differences: Heterotheca subaxillaris is also called camphorweed but has conspicuous yellow ray florets. Conoclinium has opposite triangular 3-veined leaves.
